research_question: When an agent appears to lose continuity after a language switch, when was task state forgotten and when was intact state routed through a different language control plane, locale asset, or evaluation contract?
decision_owner: Conversational-agent owners deciding whether to repair memory, localization/control configuration, or evaluation.
worlds: W1: Persistent task facts or evolving constraints were lost, overwritten, or retrieved incorrectly.
W2: Task state remained intact, but the selected/detected language changed retrieval, response, entity, fulfillment, or flow behavior.
W3: Long-horizon task or judge design labels a general execution failure as memory discontinuity.
discriminator: A revision-pinned multi-turn replay that snapshots persistent state before a language switch, logs language-control variables and selected locale assets, and independently adjudicates intended actions after the switch.
falsifier: The continuity error vanishes when language-control routing is held fixed despite unchanged memory, or persists identically across languages after control and evaluator normalization.
scope: Method-free R0 problem framing; any benchmark, replay system, or visualization is an instrument.
does_not_establish: Review-only source reduction; no gap, novelty, prevalence, proposal, or lifecycle transition is established.
